correctness.rationale: The support is continuous circle, real even, constant term 1. Evaluating any feasible 1+a cos(t)+b cos(mt)+c cos(2mt) at t=pi and t=pi-2pi/(3m) cancels b,c after weighting 1+2, so a<=3/(1+2u), u=cos(2pi/(3m)). In the construction, after t=pi-phi and y=cos(m phi), one has cos((arccos y)/m)>=cos(phi) for phi in [0,pi], so P>=R(y)-g(y) where g(y)=A cos(arccos(y)/m) and R(y)=1-C+B y+2C y². Exact coefficient identities B+C=A-1 and B-2C=q force R(1)=g(1), R(-1/2)=g(-1/2) and R'(-1/2)=g'(-1/2). For alpha=1/m in (0,1), every nonconstant coefficient of the hypergeometric expansion of cos(alpha arccos y) in (1-y)/2 is negative; applying three y-derivatives gives third_derivative_g(y)>0 on (-1,1), including one-sided continuous endpoints. Therefore the quadratic Hermite remainder g-R=(third_derivative_g(xi)/6)(y-1)(y+1/2)^2<=0, proving circle nonnegativity. Equality in the dual bound forces vanishing at both contacts and zero derivative at the interior contact, giving unique B,C by two independent linear equations. Independently checked cancellation, contacts and positivity across 20,001 points for m=2,3,4,7,13,35; sampling corroborates but cannot prove the all-m Hermite argument.
residual_risks: Hermite remainder uses full sign on (-1,1); numerical grid checks alone are not an all-circle or all-m proof.
The m=2 instance is known exact {1,2,4} sparse support and is not novel by itself.

value.rationale: A natural sparse positive-definite extremal family is solved for every m with a sharp analytic closed form and a unique extremizer. The dual two-contact certificate and Hermite majorization give a reusable structural method and a sharp coefficient for infinitely many distinct supports, a motivated extension beyond prior isolated m=2 and qualitative augmentation. Neither a textbook coefficient exercise nor a random finite slice.
residual_risks: The work does not settle arbitrary pairs of higher frequencies or more harmonics.

final_claim: For every integer m>=2, the sharp first-harmonic coefficient of every nonnegative real cosine polynomial supported on {0,1,m,2m} is A_m=3/(1+2 cos(2pi/(3m))); the displayed explicit Hermite-contact polynomial is the unique maximizer.
limitations: All-m proof depends on strict positivity of third derivative of the hypergeometric cosine function; finite checks m<=200 are only diagnostics.
The same support for m=2 is already solved; no independent novelty claim made for that instance.
